{{Update|date=September 2024}}

The Expenditure and Food Survey (EFS) is a [[statistical survey]] conducted by the [[Office for National Statistics]] (ONS) and the [[Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs]] (DEFRA), which collects data on private [[household]] expenditure and food consumption in [[Great Britain]]. The EFS is now known as the [[Living Costs and Food Survey]].<ref>[http://discover.ukdataservice.ac.uk/series/?sn=2000028 Living Costs and Food Survey], UK Data Service, retrieved 8 November 2013</ref>

== History == 
From 1957 until 2001, two separate surveys were conducted each year: the [[Family Expenditure Survey]] (FES) and the [[National Food Survey]] (NFS). These were later combined into the Expenditure and Food Survey (EFS), fully replacing the previous surveys. The survey is conducted by the ONS, with DEFRA sponsoring the food data component.<ref>[http://discover.ukdataservice.ac.uk/series/?sn=2000028 Living Costs and Food Survey catalogue description], UK Data Service, retrieved 8 November 2013</ref>

The survey design is based on the original FES, with notable changes, including the introduction of the [[European Standard Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose]] (COICOP). Another change involved adopting new processing software, [[SPSS]], which has impacted the structure of the datasets.<ref>[http://www.esds.ac.uk/government/docs/efsguide.pdf Introductory Guide to the Living Costs & Food and Expenditure & Food Surveys, (PDF)], Economic and Social Data Service, retrieved 8 November 2013</ref>

In 2006, the EFS transitioned from a financial year system to a calendar year system. As of January 2008, the EFS became known as the Living Costs and Food (LCF) module of the [[Integrated Household Survey]] (IHS).<ref>[http://discover.ukdataservice.ac.uk/series/?sn=2000028 Living Costs and Food Survey catalogue description], UK Data Service, retrieved 8 November 2013</ref>

In 2008, the Expenditure and Food Survey (EFS) was integrated into the Integrated Household Survey (IHS) and renamed the '''Living Costs and Food Survey'''. The EFS was created by combining the Family Expenditure Survey (FES) and the National Food Survey (NFS) in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Living Costs and Food Survey - Office for National Statistics |url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/personalandhouseholdfinances/incomeandwealth/methodologies/livingcostsandfoodsurvey |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=www.ons.gov.uk}}</ref>

In the fiscal year ending in March 2023, the response rate for LCF in the UK was 22%, a decrease of 5% from the previous year. This decline was attributed to the COVID-19 pandemic and the shift to telephone interviews. The ONS is taking steps to improve data quality, including increasing the number of interviewers and planning to integrate electronic data sources by 2025. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/ |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref>

== Methodology and Scope == 
The survey consists of a comprehensive household [[questionnaire]], an individual questionnaire for each adult over 16 years of age, a personal expenditure diary kept by each individual over two weeks, and a simplified diary kept by children aged seven to 15.<ref>[http://www.statistics.gov.uk/ssd/surveys/expenditure_food_survey.asp/ ONS Expenditure and Food Survey key facts] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090911145505/http://www.statistics.gov.uk/ssd/surveys/expenditure_food_survey.asp |date=2009-09-11}}, retrieved September 14, 2009</ref>

== Survey Results == 
The data collected in the EFS serves multiple purposes, but it is primarily used for the [[Retail Prices Index]], [[National Accounts]] estimates of household expenditure, analysis of the effects of taxes and benefits, and tracking trends in nutrition.

== Data Access == 
Data from the Living Costs and Food Survey (2008 to present), as well as from the Expenditure and Food Survey (2001 to 2007), is available for research and teaching use from the [[UK Data Service]] [http://ukdataservice.ac.uk/get-data website].
